events.before: Resources / Supplier Shop Tips / How to Optimize Your Xometry Profile for More Visibility How to Optimize Your Xometry Profile for More Visibility Written by Tricia Contreras 5 min read Published September 2, 2026 A complete, up-to-date shop profile is your most powerful tool for getting access to pre-matched Xometry jobs — it determines which jobs reach your Job Board and how much of your capacity gets put to work. Xometry helps its manufacturing Partners turn open capacity into revenue by matching shops’ capabilities and certifications to the best-fit jobs, from rapid prototypes to mass production. Your shop’s profile is the key that unlocks all of your potential jobs. Read on to learn how your profile determines which jobs you see on your Job Board, how to complete your profile, and how certain elements can boost your visibility to Xometry’s internal matching algorithm and high-value RFQ opportunities. Why Your Profile Determines Job Matching Access to a consistent flow of pre-matched jobs is one of the top reasons to be a Xometry Manufacturing Partner . After a Xometry customer places an order, that job appears on the Job Board for Partners that meet the manufacturing, certification, and inspection requirements. An incomplete or outdated profile directly limits which jobs a Partner is eligible for, and what they see on their Job Board. “Having an incomplete profile reduces the potential number of job offers a Partner can receive,” said Kacey Bennett, partner engagement manager at Xometry. “Adding all of their certifications and processes to their profile allows Partners to receive more specialized offers that maximize their shop capacity. If they don’t list a capability on their profile, they won’t get matched with a job that requires it.” Try Xometry's Instant Quoting Engine® Test-drive a sample part to get instant pricing and DFM analysis Launch Demo Complete Your Shop Capabilities Profile To complete or update your shop profile, log in to Workcenter and click the gear icon in the upper-right corner. Select Shop Capabilities, and from there you can add or update the following capabilities. Processes: Which processes is your shop equipped to handle? Xometry offers customers more than 21 processes —the more capabilities your shop has, the more jobs you’ll be eligible for. Subprocesses: Make sure you go into as much detail as possible when adding processes to your profile. Don’t forget to add subprocesses such as roll forming for sheet metal and grinding for CNC machining. Materials: Xometry customers can choose from more than 200+ materials when ordering custom parts. Listing all the materials your shop can process makes your profile better reflect your capabilities, but you’ll still be able to view jobs that might include materials that aren’t listed on your profile. Machines: Machines are the heart of your shop — make sure you add them to your shop profile! Updating your profile when you add a new machine to your shop ensures that you can get a return on your investment by filling open capacity and putting that machine to work. Adding your certifications to your profile is simple — just upload your certificates, and a member of the Xometry Partner team will validate and approve them. Certifications Certifications give customers confidence that Xometry Partners can handle the demands of their specific industries, from aerospace and defense to automotive and medical. Having in-demand certifications can elevate your shop to a higher tier in the Xometry Manufacturing Partner Network, making you eligible for higher-value jobs. On average, certified shops earn 6x more than shops without certifications. Certified Partners experience a significant increase in both the number of job offers and average job value. Adding your certifications to your profile is simple — just upload your certificates, and a member of the Xometry Partner team will validate and approve them. You’ll get a reminder to update your certifications before they need to be renewed, so you don’t lose out on any jobs because of an expired certification. First/Formal Inspection Training Completing a First Article Inspection Report or a Formal Inspection Report is another way to build customer confidence and make your shop eligible for more high-level jobs. These forms will be available on your Job Board if a job requires them. If you need any guidance for filling them out, check out this article or join Xometry’s Quality Support Hour , hosted Monday through Friday from 3:00–4:00 pm ET. QMS in a Box QMS certifications are the gold standard for documenting security and compliance, but if your shop doesn’t have a certain certification, you can still qualify for Xometry jobs. To support our Partners who are not third-party accredited and wish to align with Xometry’s requirements for accessing more complex work, Xometry offers comprehensive quality management system (QMS) guidance and templates — a starter “QMS in a box.” This guide can help you establish a QMS foundation or enhance your existing QMS to meet Xometry’s expectations. Based on the level completed, you may qualify for a higher tier and will become eligible for higher-value jobs. Partner Success Score and Outsourcing Tier Eligibility When you log in to Workcenter, your dashboard automatically displays your up-to-date Partner Success Score (PSS). Your PSS is based on all activities in the last 90 days or the last 20 jobs, whichever represents the most job volume. The quality and timeliness of your work determine your score, and a higher score opens you up to a higher volume of Xometry jobs. Maintaining a high PSS makes you eligible for a higher job volume, so if something looks off with your score, you can request a review in Workcenter through the Scorecard page by clicking “Request Review” next to any of the jobs impacting your score. Learn more about your PSS score here . A complete, up-to-date shop profile is your most powerful tool for getting access to pre-matched Xometry jobs — it determines which jobs reach your Job Board and how much of your capacity gets put to work. Take a few minutes today to review your processes, materials, machines, and certifications in Workcenter, and start seeing the results on your Job Board. events.before: Resources / Supplier Shop Tips / When to Invest in New Manufacturing Equipment When to Invest in New Manufacturing Equipment Written by Joel Schadegg 3 min read Published October 6, 2026 Considering a new machine for your shop? Learn the signals to watch for and what to weigh before you move forward. Knowing when to buy a machine rarely comes down to a single factor. The better indicator is what your shop is already telling you: how often machines go down, repair costs, how booked your shop is, and whether you can get the right work to pay off your investment. This article covers the signals to look for and considerations to keep in mind when you're thinking about adding a new piece of equipment to your shop. Signs It's Time to Invest in New Equipment First off, you'll want to look at patterns over the year. Don't let one bad month convince you it's time to sink money into brand-new gear. These are the four signs to be most aware of: Rising Downtime and Breakdowns Look at the last 12 months of downtime. If the same machine keeps stopping and the same components keep failing, repairs are buying time, not reliability. Continued repeat failures on a machine you already fixed are your cue to start looking for a replacement. Climbing Maintenance Costs Add up those repairs, service calls, and replacement parts for each machine. Annual maintenance commonly benchmarks at 2-5% of replacement value. A machine well above that and still climbing, or a rebuild quote nearing over half the replacement cost, is hard to justify. Utilization Above a Healthy Range Many job shops run at 60-65% spindle utilization, and strong shops aim for 80%. If a machine stays loaded at the top of that range and you're still running overtime or passing on work, it's a sign you've outgrown it. Spare Parts Becoming Hard to Source Past 15 years or so, controls and drives get harder to find. Age alone isn't the test; plenty of 20+ year-old machines run fine. If the only source for a board is the secondary market and lead times keep stretching, that's a signal. Looking for A Steady Work Stream? Become A Supplier Weigh Utilization and ROI Before You Buy Before you cut a PO, check whether the capacity is already on your floor. Idle time from changeovers, tool prep, and first-article approvals hides more spindle hours than most shops expect, and recovering them costs far less than a machine. If the purchase still holds up, run a payback calculation: total investment (machine, installation, tooling, training) divided by the annual net benefit. Being under three to four years is generally considered strong. Be honest about run hours, since an inflated estimate makes your hourly cost look better than it is. Many owners also ask how many hours a month the machine needs to cover its payment. Buy to fix a problem you can name, not the biggest machine you can finance. Try Xometry's Instant Quoting Engine® Test-drive a sample part to get instant pricing and DFM analysis Launch Demo It was always drilled into me that you don't buy more equipment until what you have is paid for or a contract comes your way that pays for the equipment up front. Jason McClure VP, Manufacturing Operations Work in hand is what makes the math safe. If you need work to keep new iron busy, the Xometry Partner Network matches jobs to your capabilities, skips the bidding process, and lets you pick what fits your capacity and expertise. Update Your Shop Capabilities Profile When You Invest If you're a Xometry supplier, don't forget to keep your shop machinery and capabilities up-to-date in Workcenter. Our job board shows work that matches your Shop Capabilities profile, so if the right type of machine isn't listed on your Machines Page, jobs that require it won't reach you. As far as job matching goes, an unlisted machine doesn't exist. Add it the week it's running, along with any subprocesses it opens up, such as grinding on the machining side or roll forming for sheet metal. Certifications and registrations work the same way. If you become ITAR-registered or obtain a new certification, such as AS9100 or ISO 9001, adding them to your profile opens access to higher-value jobs that go to qualified shops. That's a bigger subject, so see how to optimize your Xometry profile for the full walkthrough. In summary, good timing comes from your own numbers: downtime, upkeep, loading, and parts. Make the case on those, buy what the work needs, and make investments when it makes sense. When you're ready to put your capacity to work, apply to the Xometry Partner Network if you're not already a supplier, and keep your shop's capabilities up to date. events.before: 7. Cast Iron Cast Iron is a ferrous material known for high compressive strength, excellent vibration damping, and good wear resistance in heavy-duty applications. The material contains high carbon content that influences hardness and brittleness across different grades (gray iron and ductile iron). Shot peening improves fatigue performance by introducing compressive residual stress that reduces crack initiation under cyclic loading conditions. The process enhances durability in components exposed to repeated stress (engine blocks, machine bases, and industrial housings). The treatment improves surface resistance to crack propagation while stabilizing stress distribution across loaded regions. Cast iron applications benefit from increased service reliability and reduced failure rates in mechanical systems exposed to vibration and repetitive loading, Cast Iron .
